12: ---
13: 
14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
261:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
262: - Quick reference
263: 
264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
265: 
266: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
270: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
271: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
272: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
273: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
274: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
275: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
276: 
277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
330: 
331: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```
335: 
336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead
340: 
341: ### Before/After Code Examples
342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right
344: 
345: **Format**:
346: ```markdown
347: ### [Pattern Name]
348: 
349: **BEFORE**: [Problem description]
350: \```[language]
351: // Bad code with issues
352: // Showing what NOT to do
353: \```
354: 
355: **AFTER**: [Solution description]
356: \```[language]
357: // Good code with fixes
358: // Showing correct approach
359: \```
360: 
361: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
362: ```
363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues
368: - "Why better" rationale
369: 
370: ### Pattern Comparison Tables
371: 
372: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios
373: 
374: **Format**:
375: ```markdown
376: ### Common Patterns
377: 
378: | Scenario     | Approach A (Wrong) | Approach B (Right) | Why Better  |
379: | ------------ | ------------------ | ------------------ | ----------- |
380: | [Scenario 1] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
382: ```
383: 
384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison
385: 
386: ### Decision Logic in Markdown
387: 
388: **Purpose**: Explicit if/then logic for workflow decisions
389: 
390: **Format**:
391: \```markdown
392: ### Decision Logic
393: 
394: \```markdown
395: IF [condition A]:
396:   → [Action/Path A]
397:   → [Expected outcome A]
398: 
399: IF [condition B]:
400:   → [Action/Path B]
401:   → [Expected outcome B]
402: 
403: IF [condition C]:
404:   → [Action/Path C]
405:   → [Expected outcome C]
406: \```
407: \```
408: 
409: **Alternative format** (decision tree):
410: \```markdown
411: \```
412: Analyze situation
413: ├─ Condition A met
414: │  └─ Execute Workflow A
415: │     └─ Expected outcome A
416: ├─ Condition B met
417: │  └─ Execute Workflow B
418: │     └─ Expected outcome B
419: └─ Condition C met
420:    └─ Execute Workflow C
421:       └─ Expected outcome C
422: \```
423: \```
424: 
425: ### Validation Checkpoints
426: 
427: **Purpose**: Named checkpoints throughout workflows
428: 
429: **Format**:
430: ```markdown
431: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
432: ```
433: 
434: **Examples**:
435: - `files_analyzed`
436: - `artifacts_filtered`
437: - `strategy_determined`
438: - `root_cause_identified`
439: 
440: **Usage**: Reference in quality checklists and debugging
441: 
442: ### Prerequisites Section
443: 
444: **Purpose**: Link to required standards and context
445: 
446: > **PLACEMENT**: Prerequisites go in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph.
447: 
448: **Format**:
449: ```markdown
450: # [Workflow Name]
451: 
452: [1-2 sentence summary only - no prerequisites here]
453: 
454: ---
455: 
456: \## 1. OVERVIEW
457: 
458: ### Prerequisites
459: Follow [standard name] for all implementations:
460: - **[Standard 1]**: [Brief description]
461: - **[Standard 2]**: [Brief description]
462: - See [standard-file.md](./standard-file.md) for complete requirements
463: ```
464: 
465: **Key Elements**:
466: - Appears in Section 1 OVERVIEW, not intro
467: - Links to other reference files
468: - Lists specific requirements
469: 
470: ### Tool Integration References
471: 
472: **Purpose**: Show MCP tool usage, script execution, asset references
473: 
474: **Format for MCP Tools**:
475: \```markdown
476: **Automated [Task] via MCP:**
477: 
478: Instead of [manual approach], use Chrome DevTools MCP:
479: 
480: \```markdown
481: 1. [Step 1]:
482:    [Use tool: mcp__chrome_devtools__tool_name]
483:    - parameter1: "value"
484:    - parameter2: value
485: 
486: 2. [Step 2]:
487:    [Use tool: mcp__chrome_devtools__tool_name]
488: \```
489: 
490: **What you'll see:**
491: - [Expected output 1]
492: - [Expected output 2]
493: 
494: **Example output:**
495: \```json
496: {
497:   "field": "value",
498:   "data": "example"
499: }
500: \```
501: \```
502: 
503: **Format for Scripts**:
504: ```markdown
505: **See also:** [script_name.js](../scripts/script_name.js) for production-ready implementation
506: ```
507: 
508: **Format for Assets**:
509: ```markdown
510: **See also:** [template-name.md](../assets/template-name.md) for complete templates
511: ```
512: 
513: ### Common Error Patterns
514: 
515: **Purpose**: Document actual errors with explanations
516: 
517: **Format**:
518: \```markdown
519: **Common [System/Browser] Errors:**
520: 
521: \```javascript
522: // [Actual error message]
523: // → [What it means]
524: // → [How to fix]
525: 
526: // [Another error message]
527: // → [What it means]
528: // → [How to fix]
529: \```
530: \```
531: 
532: **Example**:
533: \```markdown
534: **Common Browser Errors:**
535: 
536: \```javascript
537: // Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'X' of undefined
538: // → Variable is undefined, check initialization
539: // → Verify element exists before accessing properties
540: 
541: // Failed to load resource: net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT
542: // → Ad blocker or browser extension blocking resource
543: // → Check Network tab, test with extensions disabled
544: \```
545: \```
546: 
547: ### Scope Limitations
548: 
549: **Purpose**: Explicitly state what's in/out of scope
550: 
551: **Format**:
552: ```markdown
553: **Note:** [Clarification of what IS supported]
554: 
555: **Out of scope:** [What is NOT supported]
556: ```
557: 
558: **Example**:
559: ```markdown
560: **Note:** All browser testing done via Chrome DevTools MCP.
561: 
562: **Out of scope:** Cross-browser testing in Firefox, Safari (MCP is Chrome-only)
563: ```
564: 
565: ### Browser Testing Checklists
566: 
567: **Purpose**: Specific viewport tests with checkboxes
568: 
569: **Format**:
570: \```markdown
571: **Browser Testing Checklist:**
572: 
573: \```markdown
574: □ Chrome (via Chrome DevTools MCP)
575: □ Mobile viewport (375px) - use DevTools emulation
576: □ Tablet viewport (768px) - use DevTools emulation
577: □ Desktop viewport (1920px)
578: □ Test viewport transitions (320px, 768px, 1920px)
579: \```
580: \```
581: 
582: ---
583: 
584: ### Phased Workflow with Checkpoints Example
585: 
586: **Purpose**: Show complete workflow with validation gates
587: 
588: **Format**:
589: ```yaml
590: implementation_workflow:
591:   phase_1_preparation:
592:     purpose: "Gather context and analyze requirements"
593:     actions:
594:       - "Read user request carefully"
595:       - "Identify affected files and systems"
596:       - "Review relevant documentation"
597:     checkpoint: "requirements_understood"
598:     validation_questions:
599:       - "Can I clearly explain what needs to be done?"
600:       - "Do I know which files will change?"
601:       - "Are there any unclear requirements?"
602: 
603:   phase_2_design:
604:     purpose: "Plan the implementation approach"
605:     depends_on: "phase_1_preparation"
606:     actions:
607:       - "Choose simplest solution that works"
608:       - "Identify potential edge cases"
609:       - "Plan validation strategy"
610:     checkpoint: "design_approved"
611:     validation_questions:
612:       - "Is this the simplest approach?"
613:       - "Have I considered edge cases?"
614:       - "Can I test this effectively?"
615: 
616:   phase_3_implementation:
617:     purpose: "Execute the planned changes"
618:     depends_on: "phase_2_design"
619:     actions:
620:       - "Make code changes following standards"

679: 
680: ---
681: 
682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---

1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only

28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |

38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.

71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.

73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```

103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!

105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes

109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose

115: 
116: ### Core Principle

135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.

142:

146:

148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources

192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?

204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.

206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic

217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```

230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:

35: 
36: ### Module-System Boundary
37: 
38: Use the module format required by the file's package boundary and loader
39: contract. Do not force one JavaScript module style across all paths.
40: 
41: | Surface | Module Pattern | Notes |
42: |---------|----------------|-------|
43: | `.js` files | Follow the nearest package `type` and loader contract | `"type": "module"` selects ESM; otherwise use the package's CommonJS boundary |
44: | `.cjs` files | CommonJS | The extension selects CommonJS |
45: | `.mjs` files | ESM | The verifier skips `'use strict'` enforcement for `.mjs` |
46: | `.opencode/plugins/*.{js,mjs,ts}` | ESM default export | Required by the OpenCode plugin loader |
47: 
48: ### CommonJS Pattern
49: 
50: Use CommonJS for `.cjs` files and `.js` files whose package boundary selects
51: CommonJS. Those files include the repository's required `'use strict'`
52: directive. ESM `.js` files follow their package boundary and also keep that
53: directive to satisfy the repository's alignment checks; it is redundant in ESM.
54: 
55: ```javascript
56: 'use strict';
57: 
58: // ... imports and implementation ...
59: 
60: module.exports = {
61:   // Exports here
62: };
63: ```
64:

66: pattern applies to legacy `.js/.cjs` utility surfaces and test runners that use
67: `require`.
68: 
69: ### Export Pattern
70: 
71: Export functions using `camelCase` names. For MCP handlers, include
72: `snake_case` aliases for backward compatibility. Do not apply this export shape
73: to OpenCode plugin paths; those use `export default`.
74: 
75: ```javascript
76: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
77: // 5. EXPORTS
78: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
79: 
80: module.exports = {
81:   // Primary exports (camelCase)
82:   loadConfig,
83:   triggerLookup,
84:   validateInput,
85: 
86:   // Backward-compatible aliases (snake_case) — MCP handlers only
87:   load_config: loadConfig,
88:   trigger_lookup: triggerLookup,
89:   validate_input: validateInput
90: };
91: ```
92:

94: system-spec-kit TypeScript source uses ESM `export` statements and compiles per
95: workspace package settings.

98: 
99: Index files re-export from multiple modules.
100: 
101: ```javascript
102: // index.js
103: 'use strict';
104: 
105: module.exports = {
106:   ...require('./config'),
107:   ...require('./database'),
108:   ...require('./search')
109: };
110: ```
111: 
112: ---
113: 
114: ## 3. ERROR HANDLING
115: 
116: ### Guard Clause Pattern
117: 
118: Validate inputs at function start. Return early on failure.
119: 
120: ```javascript
121: function processData(input, options) {
122:   // Guard clauses first
123:   if (!input || typeof input !== 'string') {
124:     return { success: false, error: 'Invalid input: expected string' };
125:   }
126: 
127:   if (!options || typeof options !== 'object') {
128:     return { success: false, error: 'Invalid options: expected object' };
129:   }
130: 
131:   // Main logic after guards pass
132:   const result = transform(input, options);
133:   return { success: true, data: result };
134: }
135: ```
136:

138: 
139: ### Try-Catch Pattern
140: 
141: Wrap async operations with specific error handling.
142: 
143: ```javascript
144: async function fetchData(query) {
145:   try {
146:     const result = await database.query(query);
147:     return { success: true, data: result };
148:   } catch (error) {
149:     logger.error(`[fetchData] Query failed: ${error.message}`);
150:     return { success: false, error: error.message };
151:   }
152: }
153: ```
154: 
155: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/search/folder-discovery.ts`
156: 
157: ### Custom Error Classes
158: 
159: Extend Error for domain-specific errors.
160: 
161: ```javascript
162: /**
163:  * Custom error for spec-folder operations.
164:  */
165: class SpecFolderError extends Error {
166:   /**
167:    * Create a SpecFolderError.
168:    * @param {string} code - Error code (e.g., 'SPEC_FOLDER_OUTSIDE_ROOT')
169:    * @param {string} message - Error description
170:    * @param {Object} [details] - Additional details
171:    */
172:   constructor(code, message, details = {}) {
173:     super(message);
174:     this.name = 'SpecFolderError';
175:     this.code = code;
176:     this.details = details;
177:     this.recoveryHint = undefined;
178:     Object.setPrototypeOf(this, SpecFolderError.prototype);
179:   }
180: }
181: 
182: module.exports = { SpecFolderError };
183: ```
184: 
185: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/config/spec-doc-paths.ts`
186:

188: 
189: Consistent error response structure.
190: 
191: ```javascript
192: // Success response
193: { success: true, data: result }
194: 
195: // Error response
196: { success: false, error: 'Error message', code: 'ERROR_CODE' }
197: ```

204:

25: 
26: ### When to Use

33: 
34: ## 2. SECURITY PATTERNS
35: 
36: ### CWE-22: Path Traversal Prevention
37: 
38: Validate and sanitize file paths.
39: 
40: ```javascript
41: const path = require('path');
42: 
43: /**
44:  * Safely resolve path within allowed directory.
45:  * @param {string} basePath - Allowed base directory
46:  * @param {string} userPath - User-provided path
47:  * @returns {string|null} Resolved path or null if invalid
48:  */
49: function safeResolvePath(basePath, userPath) {
50:   // Normalize and resolve
51:   const resolvedBase = path.resolve(basePath);
52:   const resolvedPath = path.resolve(basePath, userPath);
53: 
54:   // Verify path stays within base
55:   if (!resolvedPath.startsWith(resolvedBase + path.sep)) {
56:     console.error(`[security] Path traversal attempt: ${userPath}`);
57:     return null;
58:   }
59: 
60:   return resolvedPath;
61: }
62: ```
63: 
64: ### CWE-400: Input Limits
65: 
66: Prevent resource exhaustion with input validation.
67: 
68: ```javascript
69: const MAX_QUERY_LENGTH = 10000;
70: const MAX_RESULTS = 100;
71: 
72: function validateSearchInput(query, options) {
73:   // Limit query length
74:   if (query && query.length > MAX_QUERY_LENGTH) {
75:     return { valid: false, error: `Query exceeds ${MAX_QUERY_LENGTH} characters` };
76:   }
77: 
78:   // Limit result count
79:   if (options.limit && options.limit > MAX_RESULTS) {
80:     options.limit = MAX_RESULTS;
81:     console.warn(`[search] Limit capped to ${MAX_RESULTS}`);
82:   }
83: 
84:   return { valid: true };
85: }
86: ```
87: 
88: ### Input Sanitization
89: 
90: ```javascript
91: /**
92:  * Sanitize string input for safe use.
93:  * @param {string} input - Raw user input
94:  * @returns {string} Sanitized string
95:  */
96: function sanitizeString(input) {
97:   if (typeof input !== 'string') {
98:     return '';
99:   }
100: 
101:   // Remove null bytes
102:   return input.replace(/\0/g, '');
103: }
104: ```

106: ---

108: ## 3. TESTING PATTERNS
109: 
110: ### Using Node.js Assert

113: const assert = require('assert');
114: 
115: // Test function
116: function testLoadConfig() {

119:   assert.ok(config, 'Config should be loaded');
120:   assert.strictEqual(config.version, '1.0.0', 'Version should match');
121:   assert.deepStrictEqual(config.features, ['a', 'b'], 'Features should match');
122: }
123: 
124: // Run tests
125: if (require.main === module) {
126:   testLoadConfig();
127:   console.log('[test] All tests passed');
128: }
129: ```
130: 
131: ### Test File Organization
132: 
133: ```javascript
134: // tests/test_config.js
135: 'use strict';
136: 
137: const assert = require('assert');
138: const { loadConfig, validateConfig } = require('../scripts/core/config');
139: 
140: describe('Config Module', () => {
141:   describe('loadConfig', () => {
142:     it('should load valid YAML config', () => {
143:       const config = loadConfig('./fixtures/valid.yaml');
144:       assert.ok(config);
145:     });
146: 
147:     it('should return null for missing file', () => {
148:       const config = loadConfig('./nonexistent.yaml');
149:       assert.strictEqual(config, null);
150:     });
151:   });
152: });
153: ```
154: 
155: ---
156: 
157: ## 4. ASYNC PATTERNS
158: 
159: ### Async/Await Style
160: 
161: Prefer async/await over callbacks and raw promises.
162: 
163: ```javascript
164: // CORRECT: async/await
165: async function fetchAndProcess() {
166:   try {
167:     const data = await fetchData();
168:     const result = await processData(data);
169:     return { success: true, data: result };
170:   } catch (error) {
171:     return { success: false, error: error.message };
172:   }
173: }
174: 
175: // AVOID: Promise chains
176: function fetchAndProcess() {
177:   return fetchData()
178:     .then(data => processData(data))
179:     .then(result => ({ success: true, data: result }))
180:     .catch(error => ({ success: false, error: error.message }));
181: }
182: ```
183: 
184: ### Parallel Operations
185: 
186: ```javascript
187: // Parallel execution
188: const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([
189:   fetchUsers(),
190:   fetchPosts()
191: ]);
192: 
193: // Sequential execution (when order matters)
194: const user = await fetchUser(id);
195: const posts = await fetchUserPosts(user.id);
196: ```
197: 
198: ---
199: 
200: ## 5. TEST FILE EXEMPTION TIER
201: 
202: CLI-only test runners, setup scripts, and similar utilities are exempt from certain quality standards because they are executed directly (not imported as modules) and serve a different purpose than library code.
203: 
204: ### Scope
205: 
206: This exemption applies to:
207: - Files in `scripts/tests/`
208: - Files in `scripts/setup/`
209: - Any file with a test runner shebang (e.g., `#!/usr/bin/env node`)
210: 
211: ### Exempted Standards
212: 
213: | Standard                           | Reason for Exemption                                           |
214: |------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
215: | `module.exports` requirement       | Test runners are executed directly, not imported by other code |
216: | Guard clause requirement           | Scripts run once at CLI level; input validation is minimal     |
217: | `[module-name]` error prefix       | Test output uses its own format (e.g., pass/fail assertions)   |
218: 
219: ### What Still Applies
220: 
221: All other quality standards remain in effect for test files, including:
222: - `'use strict'` directive
223: - JSDoc documentation for non-trivial functions
224: - Error handling with try-catch for async operations
225: - Security patterns (path traversal, input limits) if handling external input
226:

228: 
229: ```javascript
230: #!/usr/bin/env node
231: 'use strict';
232: 
233: const assert = require('assert');
234: const { loadConfig } = require('../core/config');
235: 
236: // No module.exports needed — this file is executed directly
237: // No guard clauses needed — CLI-level script
238: // No [module-name] prefix needed — test output format
239: 
240: const config = loadConfig('./fixtures/valid.yaml');
241: assert.ok(config, 'Config should load successfully');
242: assert.strictEqual(config.version, '1.0.0');
243: 
244: console.log('PASS: All config tests passed');
245: ```

249: ## 6. SKILLED PLUGIN EXEMPTION TIER
250: 
251: OpenCode plugin entrypoints and helper modules are exempt from the CommonJS export standard because the OpenCode plugin loader requires ESM default exports. This exemption is narrow and does not relax other JavaScript quality standards.
252: 
253: ### Scope
254: 
255: This exemption applies to:
256: - `.opencode/plugins/*.{js,mjs,ts}`
257: 
258: ### Exempted Standards
259: 
260: | Standard                           | Reason for Exemption                                                               |
261: |------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
262: | `module.exports` requirement       | OpenCode plugin loader requires ESM default export per `@opencode-ai/plugin/dist/index.d.ts` |
263: 
264: ### What Still Applies
265: 
266: All other quality standards remain in effect for OpenCode plugin files, including:
267: - JSDoc on exports
268: - Guard clauses
269: - Security patterns
270: - Error handling
271: - Bracketed logging if logging exists
272: - Numbered ALL-CAPS section dividers
273: - `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` constants
274: - `camelCase` functions
275: 
276: ### Runtime Output — Never Overlay the TUI
277: 
278: OpenCode's TUI paints plugin `stdout`/`stderr` onto the prompt input line, where it sticks until a redraw and corrupts the interactive session. Plugins therefore MUST NOT write user- or agent-facing output to the console (`console.log`/`warn`/`error`, `process.stdout`/`stderr.write`). 279: 
280: | Channel | Use for |
281: |---|---|
282: | `experimental.chat.system.transform` — push a **bounded** string to `output.system` | Agent-actionable notices the model should see and can act on or relay |
283: | Append-only log file (e.g. `.skilled/logs/*.log`, fail-open) | Durable operator/audit record |
284: | A plugin `tool` the agent can call | On-demand status the user explicitly requests |
285:

287: 
288: ### Brief Example

292: // MODULE: Example OpenCode Plugin
293: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
294: 'use strict';
295: 
296: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
297: // 1. IMPORTS
298: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
299: 
300: import { tool } from '@opencode-ai/plugin';
301: 
302: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
303: // 2. CONSTANTS
304: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
305: 
306: const PLUGIN_ID = 'example-plugin';
307: 
308: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
309: // 3. PLUGIN FACTORY
310: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
311: 
312: /**
313:  * Create the example OpenCode plugin hooks.
314:  *
315:  * @param {Object} ctx - OpenCode plugin context
316:  * @param {Object} [options] - Plugin options
317:  * @returns {Promise<Object>} Hooks object for the OpenCode plugin loader
318:  */
319: export default async function ExamplePlugin(ctx, options = {}) {
320:   return {
321:     tool: {
322:       example_status: tool({
323:         description: 'Show example plugin status',
324:         args: {},
325:         async execute() {
326:           return `plugin_id=${PLUGIN_ID}`;
327:         },
328:       }),
329:     },
330:   };
331: }
332: ```

14: # JavaScript Style Guide
15: 
16: Formatting standards and naming conventions for JavaScript files in the OpenCode development environment.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Defines consistent styling rules for JavaScript files to ensure readability, maintainability, and alignment across all OpenCode JavaScript code.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: Use when writing, reviewing, or resolving style questions for JavaScript files.
29: 
30: ### Use Cases
31: 
32: - Writing new JavaScript files
33: - Reviewing JavaScript code for consistency
34: - Resolving style disagreements in code review
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. FILE HEADER FORMAT
39: 
40: All JavaScript files MUST begin with a module header identifying the module,
41: using the divider form below. Module syntax follows the nearest package
42: boundary and loader contract: `.cjs` is CommonJS, `.mjs` is ESM, and `.js`
43: follows the nearest package's `type`. OpenCode plugin paths use their ESM
44: loader contract.
45: 
46: ### Template
47: 
48: ```javascript
49: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
50: // MODULE: [Module Name]
51: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
52: ```
53: 
54: ### Requirements
55: 
56: - Divider width: 67 box-drawing characters after `// `
57: - Module name: after `MODULE:` on the middle line
58: - A shebang line may precede the header in an executable script
59: - Immediately followed by `'use strict';` for `.js/.cjs` files, as required by
60:   this repository's alignment checks; it is redundant in ESM `.js` files
61: - `.mjs` files do not require `'use strict'`; ESM `.js` plugin files follow the
62:   `.js` requirement above
63: - The older 78-character `╔═╗` box is accepted where it already exists; do not
64:   introduce it in new files
65: 
66: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/lib/dist-freshness.cjs:1-4`,
67: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/generate-trigger-index.mjs:1-4`
68: 
69: ---
70: 
71: ## 3. USE STRICT DIRECTIVE
72: 
73: Every `.js` and `.cjs` JavaScript file MUST include the strict mode directive.
74: This repository convention also applies to ESM `.js` files, where it is
75: redundant because modules are strict by definition. Do not add it to `.mjs`
76: files; the alignment verifier intentionally skips `.mjs` enforcement.
77: 
78: ```javascript
79: 'use strict';
80: ```
81: 
82: **Placement**: Immediately after file header, before any other code.
83: 
84: **Evidence**: `verify_alignment_drift.py` skips `.mjs`; CommonJS-style JS
85: helpers still use `'use strict'`.
86: 
87: ---
88: 
89: ## 4. SECTION ORGANIZATION
90: 
91: Large files are organized using numbered section dividers.
92: 
93: ### Section Divider Template
94: 
95: ```javascript
96: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
97: // 1. [SECTION NAME]
98: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
99: ```
100: 
101: ### Standard Section Order
102: 
103: | Order | Section Name     | Purpose                           |
104: |-------|------------------|-----------------------------------|
105: | 1     | IMPORTS          | Module dependencies               |
106: | 2     | CONSTANTS        | Configuration values, magic numbers |
107: | 3     | HELPERS          | Internal utility functions        |
108: | 4     | CORE LOGIC       | Main implementation               |
109: | 5     | EXPORTS          | Module public interface           |
110: 
111: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/core/config.ts`
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 5. NAMING CONVENTIONS
116: 
117: ### Function Names
118: 
119: **Style**: `camelCase`
120: 
121: ```javascript
122: // CORRECT
123: function loadConfig(path) { }
124: function memorySearch(query, options) { }
125: function validateInput(data) { }
126: 
127: // INCORRECT
128: function load_config(path) { }     // snake_case
129: function LoadConfig(path) { }      // PascalCase
130: function load-config(path) { }     // kebab-case (invalid syntax)
131: ```
132: 
133: **Evidence**: MDN Web Docs, Airbnb Style Guide, Node.js core APIs
134: 
135: ### Constant Names
136: 
137: **Style**: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`
138: 
139: ```javascript
140: // CORRECT
141: const MAX_RETRIES = 3;
142: const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 5000;
143: const SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT = 30000;
144: 
145: // INCORRECT
146: const maxRetries = 3;       // camelCase
147: const max_retries = 3;      // snake_case (reserved for variables)
148: ```
149: 
150: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/core/config.ts`
151: 
152: ### Class Names
153: 
154: **Style**: `PascalCase`
155: 
156: ```javascript
157: // CORRECT
158: class SpecFolderError extends Error { }
159: class ConfigLoader { }
160: class TriggerIndex { }
161: 
162: // INCORRECT
163: class specFolderError { }   // camelCase
164: class spec_folder_error { } // snake_case
165: ```
166: 
167: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/config/spec-doc-paths.ts`
168: 
169: ### Variable Names
170: 
171: | Scope        | Style        | Example                          |
172: |--------------|--------------|----------------------------------|
173: | Local        | `camelCase`  | `const searchResults = []`       |
174: | Module-level | `camelCase`  | `const dbPath = '...'`           |
175: | Parameters   | `camelCase`  | `function search(query, maxResults)` |
176: 
177: ### Boolean Names
178: 
179: **Style**: `camelCase` with `is`/`has`/`can`/`should` prefix
180: 
181: ```javascript
182: // CORRECT
183: const isValid = true;
184: const hasResults = items.length > 0;
185: const canProceed = !isBlocked;
186: const shouldRetry = attempts < MAX_RETRIES;
187: 
188: // INCORRECT
189: const is_valid = true;       // snake_case
190: const valid = true;          // ambiguous
191: ```
192: 
193: ### Naming Summary Table
194: 
195: | Element          | Convention         | Example                |
196: |------------------|--------------------|------------------------|
197: | Functions        | `camelCase`        | `loadConfig`           |
198: | Constants        | `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` | `MAX_RETRIES`          |
199: | Classes          | `PascalCase`       | `MemoryError`          |
200: | Local variables  | `camelCase`        | `searchResults`        |
201: | Module variables | `camelCase`        | `dbConnection`         |
202: | Parameters       | `camelCase`        | `queryText`            |
203: | Booleans         | `is`/`has`/`can`   | `isValid`, `hasItems`  |
204: 
205: ---
206: 
207: ## 6. FORMATTING RULES
208: 
209: ### Indentation
210: 
211: - **Size**: 2 spaces
212: - **Tabs**: Never use tabs
213: 
214: ```javascript
215: // CORRECT (2 spaces)
216: function example() {
217:   if (condition) {
218:     return value;
219:   }
220: }
221: 
222: // INCORRECT (4 spaces or tabs)
223: function example() {
224:     if (condition) {
225:         return value;
226:     }
227: }
228: ```
229: 
230: ### Braces
231: 
232: **Style**: K&R (opening brace on same line)
233: 
234: ```javascript
235: // CORRECT (K&R style)
236: if (condition) {
237:   // code
238: } else {
239:   // code
240: }
241: 
242: function example() {
243:   // code
244: }
245: 
246: // INCORRECT (Allman style)
247: if (condition)
248: {
249:   // code
250: }
251: ```
252: 
253: ### Semicolons
254: 
255: **Rule**: Always use semicolons
256: 
257: ```javascript
258: // CORRECT
259: const value = 42;
260: return result;
261: 
262: // INCORRECT (ASI-dependent)
263: const value = 42
264: return result
265: ```
266: 
267: ### Quotes
268: 
269: **Rule**: Single quotes for strings
270: 
271: ```javascript
272: // CORRECT
273: const message = 'Hello world';
274: const template = `Value: ${value}`;  // Template literals OK
275: 
276: // INCORRECT
277: const message = "Hello world";  // Double quotes
278: ```
279: 
280: ### Line Length
281: 
282: - **Soft limit**: roughly 100 to 120 characters, per the shared formatting rule
283: - **Preferred**: 80 characters
284: - **Exception**: URLs and long strings
285: 
286: ---
287: 
288: ## 7. COMMENTING RULES
289: 
290: ### Principles
291: 
292: 1. **Quantity limit (Skilled surface setting):** Maximum 3 comments per 10 lines of code, this surface's budget for the shared comment-density rule (see [naming and commenting](../shared/universal-patterns/naming-and-commenting.md))
293: 2. **Focus on purposeful semantics:** Explain WHY something is done, not WHAT it does
294: 3. **Focus on WHY, not WHAT:** Explain intent, constraints, reasoning
295: 4. **No commented-out code:** Delete unused code (git preserves history)
296: 
297: ### Comment Examples
298: 
299: Use plain comments that explain reasoning:
300: 
301: - `// Reasoning for non-obvious choice`
302: - `// Precondition/invariant check`
303: - `// State that must always hold`
304: - `// SEC: security note tied to a stable standard (CWE-###)`
305: - `// Safety, performance, or reliability constraint`
306: 
307: ### Capitalization
308: 
309: All comment text MUST start with a capital letter:
310: 
311: ```javascript
312: // Reverse order preserves dependency chain     // correct
313: // reverse order preserves dependency chain     // wrong
314: ```
315: 
316: **Exceptions**: `eslint-disable` directives, `@ts-` annotations, and inline code references.
317: 
318: ### Reference Comments
319: 
320: Use a bracketed module prefix for inline comments:
321: 
322: ```javascript
323: // [module-name] Description of what this does
324: ```
325: 
326: Cite only durable references, never a spec-folder-internal id. Comments must not embed a spec folder/number, task/checklist/requirement id (`T###`, `CHK-###`, `REQ-###`), feature-catalog entry, ADR id, or ticket id; see [`../shared/universal-patterns/naming-and-commenting.md`](../shared/universal-patterns/naming-and-commenting.md) §4 and [`../../../sk-code-quality/references/code-style-guide.md`](../../../sk-code-quality/references/code-style-guide.md) §4 "No ephemeral-artifact pointers".
327: 
328: ```javascript
329: // GOOD — durable WHY, no ephemeral id
330: // Causal Memory Graph handlers: drift-why, causal-link, causal-stats, causal-unlink
331: // Recover pending writes on startup so a crash cannot lose data
332: // SEC: sanitize input to prevent stored XSS (CWE-79)
333: ```
334: 
335: ### Function Purpose Comments
336: 
337: Single line above function describing intent:
338: 
339: ```javascript
340: // Load configuration from YAML file, merging with defaults
341: // Returns validated config object or throws on invalid schema
342: function loadConfig(configPath) { }
343: 
344: // Calculate weighted memory score using decay function
345: // Higher scores indicate more recent and relevant memories
346: function calculateMemoryScore(memory, currentTime) { }
347: ```
348: 
349: ### Inline Comments (WHY, Not WHAT)
350: 
351: **Good examples (explain reasoning):**
352: 
353: ```javascript
354: // Skip if already initialized to prevent double-binding
355: if (window[INIT_FLAG]) return;
356: 
357: // Sort by recency so newest memories surface first
358: results.sort((a, b) => b.timestamp - a.timestamp);
359: 
360: // Add timeout to prevent hang on unresponsive database
361: const timeout = new Promise((_, reject) =>
362:   setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('Timeout')), 30000)
363: );
364: 
365: // Close DB connection on all control paths
366: try {
367:   await processBatch(items);
368: } finally {
369:   db.close();
370: }
371: ```
372: 
373: **Bad examples (narrate implementation):**
374: 
375: ```javascript
376: // Set the value to 42
377: const value = 42;
378: 
379: // Loop through items
380: for (const item of items) { }
381: 
382: // Check if result exists
383: if (result) { }
384: 
385: // Add item to array
386: items.push(item);
387: ```
388: 
389: ### Debug Logging Pattern
390: 
391: ```javascript
392: // Conditional logging for debug mode
393: const DEBUG = false;
394: const LOG_PREFIX = '[ModuleName]';
395: 
396: function log(...args) {
397:   if (DEBUG) {
398:     console.log(LOG_PREFIX, ...args);
399:   }
400: }
401: 
402: // Usage
403: log('Initialized with config:', config);
404: log('Processing batch:', batch.length, 'items');
405: ```
406: 
407: ### JSDoc Comments
408: 
409: Required for all exported functions. See `quality-standards.md` for full JSDoc format.
410: 
411: ```javascript
412: /**
413:  * Brief description of function purpose.
414:  *
415:  * @param {string} query - Search query text
416:  * @param {Object} options - Search options
417:  * @param {number} options.limit - Maximum results to return
418:  * @returns {Array} Array of search results
419:  */
420: function search(query, options = {}) {
421:   // implementation
422: }
423: ```
424: 
425: ### TODO Comments
426: 
427: Format for tracking incomplete work.
428: 
429: ```javascript
430: // TODO: [description of work needed]
431: // FIXME: [description of bug to fix]
432: ```
433: 
434: ---
435: 
436: ## 8. IMPORT ORDER
437: 
438: Organize imports in three groups with blank lines between.
439: 
440: ```javascript
441: 'use strict';
442: 
443: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
444: // 1. IMPORTS
445: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
446: 
447: // Node.js built-ins
448: const fs = require('fs');
449: const path = require('path');
450: 
451: // Third-party modules

453: const sqlite = require('better-sqlite3');
454: 
455: // Local modules

457: const logger = require('../utils/logger');
458: ```
